title: Pterosaurs: Not Flying Dinosaurs
summary: Josh and Chuck explain pterosaurs, the flying reptiles of the Mesozoic that were not dinosaurs or birds and were not all pterodactyls. They cover their size and wingspan, the history of fossil discovery (Cosimo Alessandro Collini, Cuvier, O. C. Marsh in Kansas), head crests and their possible uses, feeding habits like pelican-style skimming, convergent evolution, quadrupedal walking, the hollow, thin bones, flight mechanics and tail loss, early misidentification as bats and birds, and the paleontology community's rivalries. The episode closes with a listener mail about foot binding in China.

segments.title: Opening banter and pterosaur introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the phrase 'batching it,' then introduce Quetzalcoatlus as a giant pterosaur and explain that pterosaurs were flying reptiles, not dinosaurs, and that pterodactyl is only one genus.

segments.title: Pterosaur classification and fossil history
segments.summary: They discuss pterosaurs' relationship to dinosaurs (archosaur group), the confusion with pterodactyls in movies, and the early fossil history: Collini's lagoon find in Germany, Cuvier's naming, and O. C. Marsh's Kansas digs. They note why pterosaur fossils are rare.

segments.title: Head crests, diet, and convergent evolution
segments.summary: The hosts describe the varied head crests and debated uses such as steering, defense, and display, and the sex-identified specimen. They discuss species with unusual shapes and a skimming, pelican-like feeding habit that evolved independently of pelicans.

segments.title: Misidentification as bats and birds, and walking posture
segments.summary: Early scientists Soemmerring and Harry Seeley wrongly linked pterosaurs to bats and birds. The hosts explain the wing finger structure differences from bats and how pterosaurs were revealed to be quadrupeds rather than standing upright.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the discussion of flight.

segments.title: Takeoff, flight mechanics, and tail loss
segments.summary: They discuss how pterosaurs likely launched from their forelimbs, compare this to birds, and describe early tailed forms versus later tailless azhdarchids, with wrist-controlled wing changes for steering and diving.

segments.title: Hollow bones, wingspan, and a private jet anecdote
segments.summary: The hosts describe the very thin, hollow, plywood-like bones and internal struts, and the large wingspans comparable to a fighter jet. A tangent follows where Chuck describes his first private jet flight, and they note the Russia visa update.

segments.title: Paleontology community and dinosaur interest
segments.summary: They discuss why dinosaurs appeal to kids, the 'golden age' of pterosaur research, and a National Geographic article describing rivalries among pterosaur paleontologists.

segments.title: Listener mail: foot binding
segments.summary: A listener from Guangdong shares that her great-great-grandmother had bound feet but bought toddler shoes and walked fine, and that the family's later generations avoided the practice. Josh and Chuck also note a pronunciation correction.
